items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the criminal procedure law, in relation to vacating records
for certain proceedings; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating
thereto
items.lawCode: Rpld & add §440.10 sub 1 ¶(k), amd §160.50, CP L (as proposed in S.6579-A & A.8420-A)
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6613

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the criminal procedure law, in
relation to vacating records for certain proceedings; and to repeal
certain provisions of such law relating thereto

 
PURPOSE:

This is a chapter amendment that makes clarifying and technical changes
to provisions of a chapter of the laws of 2019 establishing procedures
for vacating and expunging certain convictions.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the chapter amendment amends the criminal procedure law to
clarify the process for vacating a past conviction when there are severe
or ongoing consequences.

Section 2 of the chapter amendment makes clarifying changes to the crim-
inal procedure law regarding expungement of records.

Section 3 of the chapter amendment makes technical changes to the crimi-
nal procedure law and clarifies the time frame during which prior
records must be expunged.

Section 4 of the chapter amendment makes clarifying changes to a
provision of the criminal procedure law regarding the process for
expunging records.

Section 5 of the chapter amendment establishes the effective date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

The criminal procedure law, as amended by the underlying bill, estab-
lishes procedures for vacating and expunging prior convictions for low-
level marihuana charges.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This chapter amendment amends certain provisions established by the
underlying bill to ensure that records are thoroughly expunged in a
timely manner and to provide a method for detailed findings of fact when
a person applies to have his or her previous convictions vacated.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Chapter amendment to a chapter of the laws of 2019. S.6579-A and
A.8420-A passed both the Senate and Assembly in June of 2019.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the same date and in the same manner as a
chapter of the laws of 2019, amending the penal law and the criminal
procedure law relating to vacating records for certain proceedings, as
proposed in legislative bills numbers S. 6579-A and A.8420-A, takes
effect.
